chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from whom he mentioned from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

Say in Baghdad: Peace be upon you, O Guardian of God. Peace be upon you, O Proof of God. Peace be upon you, O Light of God in the darknesses of the earth. Peace be upon you, O he whom God manifested in his affair. I have come to you acknowledging your right and opposing your enemies, so intercede for me with your Lord, and supplicate to God, and ask for your need, and you will be safe. And conclude with this greeting upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when visiting the Imam in Baghdad?
ai.summary: This Ziyarah, recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, is traditionally recited by pilgrims in Baghdad, reflecting the historical centrality of the city during the Minor and Major Occultation periods. It highlights the Imam’s role as the 'Proof of God' (Hujjat Allah) and 'Light of God' (Nur Allah), emphasizing his authority to intercede and his enmity toward the enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt. The supplication concludes with a specific salutation to Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir), linking the living Imam to the broader lineage of Imams.
